search.title: Scene Scout: Search
search.intro: Scene Scout searches your indexed episodes by description rather than by filename. Type what you remember of a scene and it finds the closest matches.
search.step1: Create or open a database in the left panel. One per series works well.
search.step2: Move it into Searching by double-clicking it, dragging it up, or right-clicking it. All databases lists everything you have; only the ones in Searching are searched.
search.step3: Press Add Episode and pick one or more videos. Indexing watches every scene once and stores a fingerprint of each, which takes a while but only happens once per episode.
search.step4: Describe the scene you want in plain language and press Enter.
search.settings: Results controls how many matches come back. Scene detection is chosen each time you add episodes.

flow.title: Scene Scout: Match
flow.intro: Match finds scenes that could come right after a clip you already have. It looks at the clip's last frame and returns the scenes in your databases that look most like it, so the cut between them feels continuous.
flow.step1: Add the databases to search to the Searching list on the left.
flow.step2: Press Import and pick a video file, or right-click a clip in your Library or in Search results and pick Find matching clips.
flow.step3: Click a match to play it in the preview pane, and export it from there as usual.
flow.tips: Drag the bar between the clip and the results to give either more room. The refresh button runs the same clip again, for example after changing which databases are searched.

info.title: Community Events
info.intro: The community is pretty huge, and editing contests often go unnoticed as a result. This page gathers them in one place so editors can find opportunities worth entering, and hosts reach the people most likely to show up. Better turnout makes for better events, and events that go well encourage the next person to run one.
info.hc: A short, fixed window. Editors get a set number of hours, usually on a single day, to make an edit from start to finish. These are lower commitment and I personally love participating in these (crptk)
info.ec: A longer format that runs at least a day and often much more. There is room to plan and refine, usually less restrictions, and the prizes tend to be bigger.
info.step1: Sign in with Discord using the Login button so you can manage the event going forward. All logins are done through Discord's official API, so we have no access to your data.
info.step2: Press Host Event and pick the format: HC for a timed contest, EC for a longer contest.
info.step3: Fill in the title, cover image, description, dates, and an invite to the Discord server where the event actually happens. Add a prize pool if there is one.
info.step4: Send it for review. A moderator checks every submission before it goes live, which usually takes a short while.
info.step5: You will get a notice once it is approved. After that you can still correct the dates, invite link, or prize pool yourself; changing the title, description, or cover sends it back for another quick review.
